The Authentic Name

Scholarly reference for Fáfnir

Younger Futhark

ᚠᛅᚠᚾᛁᚱ

The name in its original Younger Futhark form. ᚠᛅᚠᚾᛁᚱ → Fáfnir. ᚠ (fé) writes both /f/ and /v/ · ᛅ (ár) writes /a/, /á/ and /æ/ · ᚾ (nauðr) writes /n/ · The spelling fafnir is a normalized phonetic reconstruction; Younger Futhark does not distinguish voiced/voiceless stops or separate short and long vowels

ASCII Constraint

FAFNIR

Stripped of its identity, the name was reduced to plain Latin letters. The original orthography — stress, length, breathing — was erased by systems that only understand A-Z.

Unicode Restoration

Fáfnir

The Unicode restoration recovers what ASCII destroyed. This is philological accuracy — not decoration. The domain encodes to Punycode, but the browser displays the truth.

Name Senses
Etymology The embracer

The name carries more than one valid sense. The primary sense is the figure or role; the etymology is the older linguistic root.

Punycode Encoding
fáfnir.com → xn--ffnir-xqa.com

The non-ASCII characters in Fáfnir are encoded while the ASCII remains visible. To the DNS, it is Punycode. To humanity, it is Fáfnir. PUNICODEX does not claim this domain is available; always verify status with a registrar.

Tier Classification

Why Fáfnir is classified as Tier-1

The Old Norse restoration ᚠᛅᚠᚾᛁᚱ preserves at least one distinctive feature its ASCII form loses — a diacritic or a distinctive letter that marks the original phonology. This makes it a single-tier Tier-1 name.
